atlas-om.0001: The least documented Gulf market in this guide: Oman’s local banks are based in Muscat, and Sohar’s port and free zone handled 72 million tonnes in 2025, but no graduate route or hiring evidence for Europeans was found, and work needs a visa arranged before you start. Read the UK’s advice on regional attacks.
atlas-om.0002: Oman was not covered by the research library before this record.
atlas-om.0003: No source read gives Muscat’s jobs by sector, graduate programmes open to foreigners, pay or tax; finance is rated only present.
atlas-om.0004: Oman visas, residence permits, labour quotas, and student routes are fully verified in visas_immigration/oman/oman_visas_immigration_guide.md.
atlas-om.0005: Sohar logistics is rated strong on the port’s own figures as reported in the press (throughput, commitments, project value), not on hiring; no employer inside the freezone was named on a page read.
atlas-om.0006: Oman publishes no governorate GDP, wage or rent series that could be read; populations are the December 2025 statistics-centre figures as reported by a newspaper, for whole governorates (Sohar is a wilayat within North Batinah).
atlas-om.0007: Country brief: Muscat and Sohar, banks, the port, graduate schemes and standing
atlas-om.0008: §1 and §3 Gulf work rules and safety (Oman is not covered separately)
atlas-om.0009: The capital, where Oman’s licensed banks are based
atlas-om.0012: two-year programme for its own staff; training aimed at "the national cadre"
atlas-om.0013: An industrial port and free zone between Muscat and Dubai
atlas-om.0015: 72 million tonnes handled, USD 968 million of new commitments
atlas-om.0017: The central bank’s list of licensed banks gives Muscat-area addresses (Ruwi, Hai Al Mina, Madinat Al Fahal, Al Khuwair) for Oman’s local banks, among them Bank Muscat, National Bank of Oman, Bank Dhofar, Oman Arab Bank, Sohar International and Ahli Bank, and for foreign banks such as Standard Chartered and HSBC.
atlas-om.0018: The UK Foreign Office reports strikes and retaliatory attacks by Iran in the region, Oman included, since 8 July 2026, and warns of flight cancellations and airspace closures; it does not advise against travel to Oman as a whole.
atlas-om.0019: Sohar Port and Freezone said in 2020 that it had attracted over OMR10.4 billion (USD 27 billion) of investment since the port opened 16 years earlier.
atlas-om.0020: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) does not rank Muscat: it is one of 22 associate centres, with 23 assessments in 24 months against the 150 needed to be listed, and a mean assessment of 630.
atlas-om.0021: At the end of 2025 Oman had 5,359,557 residents, 43.3% of them expatriates; Muscat governorate had 1,532,234 (936,383 expatriates and 595,851 Omanis) and North Batinah, where Sohar is, 940,999.
atlas-om.0022: Oman’s real GDP was OMR 39.30 billion in 2025, up 2.4%; non-oil activities rose 3.1% to OMR 28.70 billion and petroleum activities 1.1% to OMR 12.02 billion.
atlas-om.0023: SOHAR Port and Freezone says its annual throughput rose from 62 million tonnes in 2019 to 72 million by the end of 2025, with 3,427 vessel calls, and that in 2025 it secured $968 million of new commitments across eight agreements; its freezone ranked third globally in fDi Intelligence’s free-zone index.
atlas-om.0024: SOHAR Port and Freezone reported cargo throughput of 52 million tonnes in the first half of 2026, up 52%, and container throughput of 545,000 TEU, up 40%; projects under way across the port and freezone are worth OMR 2.62 billion.
atlas-om.0025: Bank Muscat’s two-year High Potential Graduate Development programme enrolled 57 of its own employees in two batches in October 2023, and the bank describes its training as developing "the national cadre".
atlas-om.0026: English is standard for multinational firms and Arabic is often required for government and local companies, according to a CV guide; an Omani labour contract must be written in Arabic in two copies, and KPMG Middle East's graduate assessments test English; no source measured the level employers require.
atlas-om.0027: Graduate recruiting in Oman runs on university fairs and autumn postings rather than a national season: the Oman Internship Fair was held on 26 January 2026 with more than 65 companies, Sohar University's Career Training Fair on 2-4 February 2026 and Sultan Qaboos University's Career Fair on 13-15 April 2026; the Oman Airports graduate programme was posted on 1 October 2025 with a deadline of 12 October 2025, and OQ's 130 graduates were onboarded by 4 February 2026.
atlas-om.0028: Oman's job-seeker rate was 3.1% in 2025 and 2.4% in June 2026 (13.2% for ages 15 to 24); among bachelor's holders it was 12.4% for women and 1.3% for men, and 0.5% for master's and doctoral holders; at the end of June 2026 Omanis held 441,737 private-sector and 392,962 government jobs, and in the Employer Survey 2025 47% of private employers had hired graduates with no work experience; no figure for expatriate graduates was found.
atlas-om.0029: Oman reserves a growing list of professions for Omanis, and junior white-collar roles are among the first: marketing specialists, sales representatives and quality-control officers are already closed to new expatriate hires, systems analysts were added from 2025 and programmers and computer engineers from 2026.
atlas-om.0030: Omanis were 21.8% of workers in private and family-run businesses in 2025, so the private market is large for foreigners, but the graduate programmes we could read (PDO, OQ, Oman Airports) are for Omanis, and a foreign graduate is mostly hired as an experienced specialist whose employer proves its Omanisation compliance.
atlas-om.0031: Direct application or recruiter, with the employer obtaining the Labour Clearance
atlas-om.0032: Expatriates were 67.1% of Oman’s 2.7 million workers in 2025 and the private sector held 68.4% of jobs, so most foreign hires come through private employers; the employer applies for the Ministry of Labour clearance, proving Omanisation compliance, and then the visa, which the library puts at 2 to 4 working weeks in practice.
atlas-om.0033: Expatriates in regulated professions (engineering, logistics, accounting) must have their qualifications assessed and approved by accredited sectoral skills units before arrival, and entry permits follow the work practice licence (Gulf News, December 2025).
atlas-om.0035: PDO’s Graduate Development Programme is for Omani staff who join with a bachelor’s degree or above and runs 2.5 to 5 years; OQ onboarded 130 graduates into its 2026 programme under an agreement with the Ministry of Labour for 600 opportunities; Oman Airports’ graduate programme (20 places, deadline 12 October 2025) was for Omani nationals only, with a GPA of at least 3.5, age 28 or under, and registration as a job seeker with the Ministry of Labour.
atlas-om.0036: KPMG Middle East’s two-year graduate development programmes (Advisory, Audit, Tax) are advertised on its Oman page without a stated nationality rule; its selection runs online application, a talent-team meeting, online assessments, an assessment centre and an offer.
atlas-om.0038: Sultan Qaboos University’s Career Fair ran on 13–15 April 2026 with Oman Arab Bank among the exhibitors and a Ministry of Labour under-secretary at the opening; Sohar University’s Career Training Fair ran on 2–4 February 2026; the Oman Internship Fair on 26 January 2026 brought more than 65 companies together for students and fresh graduates from four partner universities, including the German University of Technology in Oman.
atlas-om.0039: SQU’s Centre for Career Guidance runs the fair and CV and interview support and gives employers lists of SQU graduates.
atlas-om.0040: Internships through a university or training institution
atlas-om.0041: The library finds no stand-alone internship status: an unpaid or privately agreed placement at a company counts as unauthorised work; a foreign trainee needs a Student Training Visa (OMR 20) requested by an authorised university or training institution, it gives only an allowance, and it cannot be converted to an employment visa inside the country.
atlas-om.0042: There is no national season: fairs fall between January and April (Oman Internship Fair on 26 January 2026, Sohar University on 2–4 February, SQU on 13–15 April), while programme postings come in autumn (the Oman Airports graduate programme was posted on 1 October 2025 with a deadline of 12 October 2025) and intakes start early in the year (OQ’s 130 graduates were onboarded by 4 February 2026).
atlas-om.0043: New expatriate hiring is closed by date, not by season: marketing specialists, sales representatives and quality-control officers from 2 September 2024, systems analysts from 1 January 2025, computer programmers and computer engineers from 1 January 2026, and web designers and operations analysts from 1 January 2027.
atlas-om.0044: For an expatriate the library finds no job-seeker visa and about 30 days of grace after studies end, and the employer’s clearance and visa take 2 to 4 working weeks in practice (7 to 10 working days officially).
atlas-om.0045: Sultan Qaboos University’s Centre for Career Guidance links the university with employers, runs the Career & Training Fair and supplies employers with lists of SQU graduates; Sohar University and the four partner universities of the Oman Internship Fair (Arab Open University, the German University of Technology in Oman, Majan University College and the National University of Science and Technology) give their students the same kind of access.
